connections.observation: s001 establishes ὅμοιον as the repeated affirmation that city and individual share likeness; s002 traces ταὐτό/αὐτά from sameness of name to sameness of εἴδη; s003 moves εἶδος from singular (justice's form) to plural (the three kinds in the soul). Held together, these three signals show likeness operating through identity of εἴδη, while εἶδος itself shifts from one to three within the very passage that affirms sameness.

s004 frames the city-soul analogy through μεῖζον and ἔλαττον; s006 traces the number three (τριττὰ γένη, τὰ τρία εἴδη, τρισὶν οὖσιν). The conjunction makes visible that the larger contains three kinds and the smaller is asked whether it contains the same three: the analogy's precision depends on matching cardinality across scale.

s007 shows φαῦλον denied and replaced by χαλεπός, which then recurs in contrasting judgments (οὐδὲν χαλεπόν, ἤδη χαλεπόν, τὰ χαλεπά); s009 distinguishes the present method from a μακροτέρα καὶ πλείων ὁδός. Together these make visible that difficulty is distributed: one claim is easy (that city and soul share kinds), another is hard (distinguishing the soul's internal agencies), and the section acknowledges a method that would resolve the difficulty but does not pursue it.

s008 pairs μέθοδος with ὁδός in close succession; s009 contrasts the present μέθοδοι with ἄλλη μακροτέρα καὶ πλείων ὁδός. The conjunction makes the etymological relation audible: μέθοδος (a following-after-a-way) is set beside ὁδός itself, and both are measured by length and sufficiency.

s010 traces directional movement (ἐμπεπτώκαμεν into an inquiry, ἄλλοθεν ἐκεῖσε ἀφῖκται from individuals into the city); s012 assigns each soul-disposition to a τόπος (Thrace/Scythia/ἄνω, παρʼ ἡμῖν, Phoenicia/Egypt). Held together, these make visible that the section's argument moves by transfer—falling into a question, arriving from elsewhere—and that the soul's three parts are located in different regions before they are located in different psychic agencies.

s011 lists three substantivized dispositions (τὸ θυμοειδές, τὸ φιλομαθές, τὸ φιλοχρήματον); s012 pairs each with a geographical τόπος; s013 notes that the spirited are located κατὰ τὸν ἄνω τόπον. Together these signals show that the three soul-parts are first differentiated by placing them in three compass-regions (north/upper, here, south/elsewhere), making the psychic division spatially articulated before it is argued.

s014 arranges three first-person plural verbs in syntactic parallel, each with a different agent (μανθάνομεν μὲν ἑτέρῳ, θυμούμεθα δὲ ἄλλῳ, ἐπιθυμοῦμεν δʼ αὖ τρίτῳ τινί); s015 frames the question as τρισὶν οὖσιν versus ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ; s018 shows πράττω used for each class doing its own work (435b ἔπραττεν) and twice for the soul's disputed action (436a–b πράττομεν). The conjunction makes visible that the section enacts in its syntax what it cannot yet demonstrate: the first-person plural is distributed across three datives as though the answer to the question has already been performed in the grammar of the question itself.

s003 moves εἶδος from singular to plural (one εἶδος of justice, three εἴδη in the soul); s006 traces the number three (γένη, εἴδη, τρισίν); s015 frames the central question as one versus three (τῷ αὐτῷ or τρισὶν οὖσιν, ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ or distributed). Held together, these show that the section's argument is structured by a repeated movement from unity to triplicity: one form becomes three kinds, one soul is asked whether it is three agents, and the question itself is framed as a choice between wholeness and partition.

s005 lists the four virtues (δικαία, σώφρων, ἀνδρεία, σοφή) as arising when three γένη each does its own work; s018 repeats πράττω for the city's classes (ἔπραττεν) and twice for the soul's possible modes of action (πράττομεν). The conjunction makes visible that the city's virtue depends on differentiated action (each kind πράττει its own), while the soul's question is whether it πράττει as one or as three—the verb that established the city's order now marks the soul's unresolved problem.

s016 specifies the desiring part through τροφή, γέννησις, and ἡδοναί; s019 frames the question's moment as ὅταν ὁρμήσωμεν. Together these make visible that the soul's partition is asked not in rest but in impulse, and that the third part's domain is bodily motion (nourishment, generation) rather than cognitive or spirited response.

s001 repeats ὅμοιον four times across 435a–b, affirming likeness and rejecting ἀνόμοιον; s004 frames the analogy through μεῖζον and ἔλαττον. Held together, these show that the larger and smaller are declared ὅμοιον in the very respect (ταὐτό) that distinguishes them in scale: likeness is secured by naming sameness, but the difference in size that makes the analogy useful is left unexamined.

s002 moves from ταὐτόν (435a, naming) to τὰ αὐτά (435b–c, 435e, the same εἴδη and ἤθη); s018 uses πράττω first for differentiated action in the city (τὸ αὑτῶν ἕκαστον ἔπραττεν) then twice for the soul's disputed unity or partition (πράττομεν). The conjunction makes visible that 'the same' shifts from shared identity of kinds to the question of whether action is unified or divided: sameness of εἴδη does not settle whether the soul acts as one or many.

elements.context: ὅμοιον, ἔφη; ὅμοιος, ἔφη; ἀληθῆ, ἔφη; πᾶσα ἀνάγκη, ἔφη; οὐ πάνυ μοι δοκοῦμεν, ἔφη; οὐκοῦν ἀγαπητόν; ἔφη; μὴ τοίνυν ἀποκάμῃς, ἔφη; καὶ μάλα, ἔφη

new_signals.observation: ἔφη recurs eight times as Glaucon's response marker; the responses vary from monosyllabic affirmation (ὅμοιον, ἀληθῆ) to qualified agreement (οὐ πάνυ μοι δοκοῦμεν) to encouragement (μὴ τοίνυν ἀποκάμῃς), tracing a movement from immediate assent to sustained engagement.

elements.context: οἳ δὴ καὶ ἔχουσι ταύτην τὴν αἰτίαν

new_signals.observation: αἰτία (435e) names the attribution peoples have (ἔχουσι ταύτην τὴν αἰτίαν) for spiritedness; αἰτιάομαι (436a) is the act of assigning love of learning to the Greek region—the noun and verb pair the passive possession of a reputation with the active attribution of a quality to a place.

elements.context: ὅτε ἐν αὐτῇ τριττὰ γένη φύσεων ἐνόντα
τὰ αὐτὰ ταῦτα εἴδη ἐν τῇ αὑτοῦ ψυχῇ
εἴτε ἔχει τὰ τρία εἴδη ταῦτα ἐν αὑτῇ
τὰ αὐτὰ ἐν ἑκάστῳ ἔνεστιν ἡμῶν εἴδη
ἐκ τῶν ἰδιωτῶν ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν ἐγγεγονέναι
θυμούμεθα δὲ ἄλλῳ τῶν ἐν ἡμῖν

new_signals.observation: The preposition ἐν recurs with shifting objects: ἐν αὐτῇ (the city), ἐν τῇ αὑτοῦ ψυχῇ and ἐν αὑτῇ (the soul), ἐν ἑκάστῳ ἡμῶν (each of us), ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν (cities), ἐν ἡμῖν (within us)—the repeated preposition marks containment while its object oscillates between singular soul, individual person, collective cities, and the plural 'us.'

elements.context: εἴτε ἔχει τὰ τρία εἴδη ταῦτα ἐν αὑτῇ εἴτε μή
εἰ τῷ αὐτῷ τούτῳ ἕκαστα πράττομεν ἢ τρισὶν οὖσιν ... ἢ ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ

new_signals.observation: The section's two central questions are both framed as disjunctions: εἴτε ... εἴτε μή (whether the soul has three kinds or not, 435c) and ἢ ... ἢ (whether we act with one agency or three, then restated as three versus the whole soul, 436a–b). The repeated either/or syntax enacts the binary form of the inquiry itself.
